tldr: AI Industry: Voters in ten states decided 41 local data-center ballot measures, and the restrictive side won nearly everywhere, by margins up to 90 percent.
International: Indonesia detained three police generals over an alleged wiretapping operation against President Prabowo, then sent more than 20,000 troops into Jakarta.
Economics: Democrats won both chambers of Congress; the dollar index fell to 101.32, gold reclaimed $4,000 and Dow futures swung to a 900-point gain.
Healthcare: Missouri voters refused 55.5 to 44.5 to restore an abortion ban, and Virginia wrote reproductive rights into its constitution 62 to 38.
Wildcard - AI Industry: Nvidia has told cloud partners worldwide to keep at least 51 percent of their business with non-Chinese customers or lose chip access.
Wildcard - Economics: Meta's debut euro bond drew a record 53 billion euros of orders, a day after a $15 billion dollar deal priced at up to 7.53 percent.
Wildcard - International Affairs: Israel certified its election 15 to 2 with 14 abstentions as Likud abstained and failed to delay the count; Netanyahu's bloc is eight seats short.
Wildcard - Healthcare: Pfizer raised full-year revenue guidance by $1.5 billion to $62-64 billion even though third-quarter sales were operationally flat.
Tech: Attackers compromised a refrigeration supplier and altered temperature settings at three French blood-plasma storage sites; no products were lost.
Trump News: After a week of rallies asking voters to pretend he was on the ballot, Trump posted that he wasn't on it and would have won a landslide if he were.

items.headline: Voters in ten states pass local bans and pauses on AI data centers
items.body: Voters decided 41 local data-center ballot measures across ten states on Tuesday, and the restrictive side won nearly everywhere results are in. Ohio alone had 21 measures in 18 municipalities, at least 14 of which approved bans or restrictions. Trenton, Ohio, banned data centers above 25 megawatts 80 percent to 20 percent; Nottingham, New Hampshire, approved a one-year permitting moratorium 90.3 to 9.7; Augusta Township, Michigan, rejected a rezoning 89.6 to 10.4. Ballotpedia counted 28 of the 41 as restrictive. Ohio already had 125 local moratoriums. Results are unofficial.
items.plain: An AI data center is a windowless building full of computers that train and run AI models. It needs land, a lot of electricity and often a lot of water, and all three are controlled locally, by zoning. A ballot measure skips the town council and asks voters directly, which is why these numbers matter: 80 and 90 percent are not close votes. The interesting part is that Ohio had already piled up 125 local pauses before anyone voted, so Tuesday did not start the backlash; it measured it.
items.why: The binding constraint on the AI build-out is shifting from chips and power contracts to local land-use votes, which a company cannot negotiate its way around, and analysts reading Tuesday's market reaction already named data-center restrictions as a risk to AI-linked shares.

items.headline: Indonesia detains three police generals over alleged wiretapping of the president, then sends troops into Jakarta
items.body: Indonesian police detained three senior police generals over an alleged illegal wiretapping operation that police say targeted President Prabowo Subianto, state officials, journalists, activists and business figures between 2025 and 2026. One is Gen. Listyo Sigit Prabowo, national police chief from 2021 until October, when he became presidential chief of staff; the president dismissed him Wednesday. Investigators allege intercepted communications were ordered deleted from the police LIMS system. The palace said the conduct could be regarded as "leading toward treason." The military said Wednesday it was sending more than 20,000 troops and personnel to Jakarta, without confirming a link to the case.
items.plain: Indonesia has about 280 million people, the fourth-largest population in the world, and Prabowo Subianto has been its president since 2024. Wiretapping means secretly recording someone's phone calls and messages; police can do it, but only by following set rules. The allegation is that senior officers did it to the president himself, and then ordered the recordings erased. Note what is alleged and what is not: three people are detained, nobody has been charged or convicted, and the government has not said why 20,000 soldiers are now in the capital.
items.why: A criminal case against the man who ran the national police, and who until last month sat in the president's own office, has put soldiers rather than police in charge of securing Jakarta, and the government has offered no explanation for the connection.

items.headline: Democratic sweep of Congress sends the dollar down and gold back above $4,000
items.body: Democrats won majorities in both chambers on Tuesday; CNN's count showed 54 Senate seats to 44 with Alaska and Mississippi uncalled, after flips including Ohio, Texas, North Carolina and Maine. Markets moved twice: Nasdaq-100 futures fell nearly 2 percent overnight as AI shares dropped in Asia, then Dow futures swung to about plus 900 points. The dollar index fell 0.39 percent to 101.32, the 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.93 percent, gold rose roughly 2.3 percent back above $4,000 and silver about 4 percent to near $52.
items.plain: The dollar index measures the dollar against a basket of other currencies, so a fall means the dollar buys less abroad. Gold and silver are what investors buy when they are less sure about currencies and government finances, so the two moves are the same bet made twice. The mechanism is simple: one party now controls the White House and the other controls Congress, so almost nothing passes without a deal. That makes big tax or spending changes unlikely, which is why bond yields eased rather than spiked. Gold is still far below its January peak of about $5,595.
items.why: Divided government turns the next two years of US fiscal policy from a program into a negotiation, and the first thing investors repriced was not equities but the currency.

items.headline: Missouri voters refuse to restore an abortion ban; Virginia writes reproductive rights into its constitution
items.body: Missouri's Amendment 3, which would have reinstated most abortion restrictions and written a ban on gender-affirming care for minors into the state constitution, failed 55.5 percent to 44.5 percent, 1,173,172 unofficial votes to 941,065. The Republican-led legislature put it on the ballot two years after Missouri became the first state to repeal an abortion ban by popular vote. Virginia approved Question 1 by 62 to 38, adding a right to reproductive care, contraception and fertility treatment to its Bill of Rights; the Family Foundation of Virginia has signaled a court challenge. Nevada's Question 6 passed with about 63 percent, the second approval the state requires.
items.plain: Most abortion rules in the United States are now set state by state, and some states let voters change the state constitution directly rather than waiting for lawmakers. Constitutional language is the prize here because a legislature can rewrite an ordinary law next session but cannot rewrite the constitution on its own. Missouri's measure bundled two things, abortion restrictions and a ban on medical treatment for transgender minors, into one question, so the vote does not separate them. Counts are unofficial until each state certifies.
items.why: Missouri's legislature asked voters the abortion question for the second time in two years and lost by a wider margin than in 2024, which sets a price for putting it on the ballot again.

items.headline: Nvidia tells cloud partners worldwide to keep most of their business non-Chinese
items.body: The Financial Times reported that Nvidia has told cloud and data-center partners to keep at least 51 percent of their business with non-Chinese customers or risk losing chip access. The instruction was passed verbally through sales teams, applies to new contracts rather than existing leases, and reaches partners globally. It targets a gap US export controls do not cover: Chinese firms including Alibaba and ByteDance have rented Nvidia capacity in Singapore and Malaysia rather than buying chips. The reporting does not establish how the 51 percent is measured or audited. Nvidia has not confirmed it, and the account rests on anonymous sources in one original report.
items.plain: US export rules stop Nvidia selling its best AI chips to Chinese companies, but they say less about a Chinese company renting time on those chips in a data center in Singapore. That gap is the whole story. Nvidia's reported answer is to lean on the landlords instead of the tenants: keep more than half your business non-Chinese or we stop selling you hardware. Treat this as credible but unconfirmed, since it comes from one outlet's anonymous sources and Nvidia has said nothing.
items.why: If accurate, enforcement of chip controls shifts from a published government rule a company can contest to a supplier's verbal condition on its own customers, with nothing written down to appeal.

items.headline: Meta's first euro bond draws a record 53 billion euros in orders
items.body: Meta raised $15 billion in a five-part dollar bond sale on Tuesday, yields running 5.85 to 7.53 percent, with orders near $58 billion. Its debut euro bond followed Wednesday and drew 53 billion euros ($59.7 billion) of demand, which Bloomberg called a record for any corporate deal in Europe. The longest dollar tranche priced 2.2 percentage points over Treasuries, about 0.9 points wider than a comparable April bond, days after S&P cut its outlook on Meta's AA- rating to negative over AI spending. Oracle raised $20 billion Monday at coupons of 7 to 8.65 percent.
items.plain: A bond is a loan from investors to a company, and the yield is what the company pays to borrow. Demand of 53 billion euros for a much smaller deal means far more lenders wanted in than could get in. The catch is in the price: Meta is paying noticeably more than it did in April, so lenders are queuing up and charging more at the same time. That happens when a borrower is seen as safe but is borrowing much more than it used to.
items.why: The AI build-out has crossed from being funded out of operating cash into being funded with debt at rising prices, which means the cost of the data-center race now shows up on balance sheets rather than only in capital-expenditure forecasts.

items.headline: Israel certifies its election over Likud's objection, leaving Netanyahu eight seats short
items.body: Israel's Central Elections Committee approved the final results of the October 27 election on Wednesday, 15 votes to two with 14 abstentions; Likud and Shas abstained, and chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg rejected Likud's request to delay certification over its claims of irregularities in the Arab vote. The committee said it found no evidence the count was altered, while noting a Shin Bet inquiry continues. Netanyahu's bloc holds 53 of 120 seats, Gadi Eisenkot's 48, Arab-led lists 19; 61 is a majority, and both leaders ruled out Arab-party partners. The new Knesset is sworn in November 10.
items.plain: Israel's parliament, the Knesset, has 120 seats, and a government needs 61 of them. No bloc has that, and the 19 seats held by Arab-led parties are the only arithmetic path to a majority, which both main contenders rejected before voting day. Certification is the formal step that turns vote counts into seats, and Likud asked to postpone it while fraud claims are examined. The committee refused, said it found no evidence the count was altered, and Likud abstained rather than voting against.
items.why: The largest party in the Knesset has declined to endorse the count that seats it, so the coming coalition fight will run alongside a dispute over whether the election itself was sound.

items.headline: Pfizer raises its 2026 forecast while overall sales stay flat
items.body: Pfizer reported third-quarter revenue of $16.6 billion on Tuesday, roughly flat year over year operationally, with reported diluted earnings of $0.56 a share and adjusted earnings of $0.87. It raised full-year revenue guidance by $1.5 billion at the midpoint to $62 billion to $64 billion and narrowed adjusted earnings guidance to $2.95 to $3.05. Launched and acquired products grew 32 percent operationally and non-COVID products 7 percent, with Nurtec up 33 percent. Adjusted earnings absorbed about $0.10 from a $650 million charge tied to an Innovent Biologics in-licensing deal.
items.plain: Guidance is the forecast a company gives investors for the year, so raising it is a claim about the months ahead, not the quarter just ended. The puzzle here is that total sales barely moved while the forecast went up. The answer is in the mix: COVID products and older drugs losing patent protection are shrinking, and recently launched or purchased drugs grew 32 percent, enough to cover the losses with room left over. "Operationally" means the figures strip out currency swings, which can flatter or flatten results on their own.
items.why: Pfizer is showing that the pipeline it bought with COVID-era cash is now replacing that revenue faster than its older drugs are losing it, which is the specific test the company has been judged on since 2023.

items.headline: Hackers raised the temperature inside French blood-plasma freezers
items.body: The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said attackers altered temperature and defrosting settings at three of its cold-storage plasma sites after compromising a supplier of refrigeration equipment. Alarms detected the anomalies and staff transferred or secured the plasma, held for transfusions and for manufacturing medicines. "No health consequences have been identified and no blood products were lost," EFS said; collection and distribution continued. Le Canard enchaine reported units were commanded from about minus 30 degrees Celsius toward 110, a figure the Associated Press accounts do not carry. France's cybersecurity agency and the Health Ministry are investigating. The attack ran overnight on November 1 and 2; no group has claimed it.
items.plain: Plasma is the liquid part of blood, used in transfusions and to make medicines, and it has to be kept frozen, so the freezer is part of the product. The attackers did not go after patient records; they went after the thermostat, and they got in through the outside company that supplies the refrigeration gear rather than through the blood service itself. What saved the plasma was boring and important: alarms noticed the temperature moving and people physically moved the bags. The 110-degree figure comes from one French outlet and is not in the wire-service accounts.
items.why: This moves hospital cyber risk from stolen data to destroyed inventory, and it shows the entry point is increasingly the equipment vendor rather than the hospital network.

items.headline: Trump spent the campaign's last week asking voters to pretend he was on the ballot, then said he wasn't
items.body: At a Kansas rally on November 1 Trump told the crowd, "I really want you to pretend I'm on the ballot," and at a South Carolina rally said, "I am on the ballot. We're all on the ballot," arguing his name raises turnout by 49.2 percent. After Democrats took both chambers he posted on Truth Social that he "wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE"; outlets rendered the wording slightly differently. A separate post said "Fox News bears responsibility for these losses." On Fox News that night he blamed Republican candidates and gas prices and said, "I don't view it as a hit on me." He told the New York Times he is "absolutely willing to accept" the results; in October he had said he would accept them "if they're honest elections."
items.plain: Midterms are the congressional elections held halfway through a presidential term, and the president's party usually loses seats, so the question is how many. Trump's own argument before the vote was that his presence on a ballot is worth a large turnout boost, which is why he asked voters to treat the election as if he were on it. After the loss he used the same claim in reverse: his absence explains the result. Both versions cannot be tested against anything except the election he himself framed as the test.
items.why: The claim that he is worth a landslide and the claim that his absence caused the defeat are one claim stated twice, and Tuesday was the measurement he proposed for it.
